scene: A nurse looks at Zestril, Capoten, Altace, and Renitec on an antihypertensive chart.
ask: Which brand-to-generic set matches the note for this -pril group?

choices.text: Zestril is lisinopril, Capoten is captopril, Altace is ramipril, and Renitec is enalapril, all ACE inhibitors.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, these -pril drugs are angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors: Zestril (lisinopril), Capoten (captopril/acepril), Altace (ramipril), and Renitec (enalapril).

choices.text: Zestril is captopril, Capoten is enalapril, Altace is lisinopril, and Renitec is ramipril.
choices.note: No. Those generics are all in the ACE inhibitor list, but the note pairs them with different brands.

choices.text: Zestril is losartan, Capoten is valsartan, Altace is candesartan, and Renitec is irbesartan.
choices.note: No. Those -sartan names are the note's angiotensin II receptor blockers, not the -pril ACE inhibitors.

choices.text: Zestril is prazosin, Capoten is terazosin, Altace is methyldopa, and Renitec is hydralazine.
choices.note: No. Those drugs are elsewhere on the antihypertensive page, not the ACE inhibitor pairs.

scene: A nurse looks at Aldomet on a chart for hypertension in pregnancy.
ask: How does the note class Aldomet and its pregnancy use?

choices.text: Aldomet is hydralazine, classed only as a hydrazinophthalazine vasodilator.
choices.note: No. Hydralazine is Apresoline on this page, not Aldomet.

choices.text: Aldomet is a selective alpha-1 blocker used for BPH and hypertension.
choices.note: No. That alpha-1 line belongs to the -osin drugs prazosin and terazosin.

choices.text: Aldomet is an ARB that blocks angiotensin II and reduces aldosterone.
choices.note: No. Blocking angiotensin II and reducing aldosterone is the note's ARB mechanism, not methyldopa.

choices.text: Aldomet is methyldopa, a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist, written as especially suitable for hypertension in pregnancy.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Aldomet (methyldopa) is a centrally acting alpha-2 agonist for moderate to severe hypertension, especially pregnancy hypertension such as gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia.

scene: A nurse looks at Minipress and Hytrin on a chart for blood pressure and prostate symptoms.
ask: What suffix, generics, and uses does the note give these alpha-1 blockers?

choices.text: The suffix is -olol; Minipress is metoprolol and Hytrin is atenolol.
choices.note: No. Metoprolol and atenolol are the note's selective beta-1 blockers, not these brands.

choices.text: The suffix is -pril; Minipress is lisinopril and Hytrin is captopril.
choices.note: No. Lisinopril and captopril are ACE inhibitors under Zestril and Capoten.

choices.text: The suffix is -osin; Minipress is prazosin and Hytrin is terazosin, selective alpha-1 blockers for BPH and hypertension.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists end in -osin; Minipress is prazosin and Hytrin is terazosin for BPH and hypertension.

choices.text: The suffix is -pine; Minipress is nifedipine and Hytrin is amlodipine.
choices.note: No. Nifedipine and amlodipine are dihydropyridine calcium blockers on this page.

scene: A nurse looks at Betaloc, Tenormin, Inderal, and Dilatrend on a beta-blocker chart.
ask: How does the note split selective and non-selective agents here?

choices.text: Selective agents are propranolol and carvedilol; non-selective agents are metoprolol and atenolol.
choices.note: No. The note puts propranolol and carvedilol on the non-selective line, not the selective beta-1 line.

choices.text: Selective beta-1 blockers are Betaloc (metoprolol) and Tenormin (atenolol); non-selective blockers are Inderal (propranolol) and Dilatrend (carvedilol).
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, -olol drugs divide into selective beta-1 blockers metoprolol and atenolol, and non-selective blockers propranolol and carvedilol.

choices.text: All four are non-DHP calcium blockers, and Dilatrend is diltiazem.
choices.note: No. Diltiazem is Herbesser/Cartia, a non-DHP calcium blocker, not carvedilol.

choices.text: Betaloc is verapamil and Tenormin is nifedipine.
choices.note: No. Verapamil is Isoptin and nifedipine is Adalat in the calcium-blocker section.

scene: A nurse looks at Norvasc and Isoptin on the same cardiac chart.
ask: How does the note contrast dihydropyridine and non-dihydropyridine calcium blockers?

choices.text: DHPs such as nifedipine, amlodipine, nimodipine, and felodipine end in -pine and act mainly on vessels; non-DHPs verapamil and diltiazem act more on the heart.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, -pine DHPs act mainly on vascular smooth muscle, while non-DHPs verapamil (Isoptin) and diltiazem (Herbesser/Cartia) act more on the heart, slowing rate and weakening contraction.

choices.text: The -pine suffix marks non-DHPs, which act mainly on the heart, and verapamil is a DHP.
choices.note: No. The note gives -pine to DHPs and places verapamil with the non-DHPs.

choices.text: Norvasc is a non-DHP and Isoptin is an ACE inhibitor ending in -pril.
choices.note: No. Norvasc is amlodipine, a DHP, and -pril is the ACE inhibitor suffix.

choices.text: Both groups block angiotensin II and reduce aldosterone.
choices.note: No. That mechanism sentence is written for ARBs ending in -sartan.

scene: A nurse looks at Apresoline beside losartan on an antihypertensive chart.
ask: Which statement matches how the note classifies these drugs?

choices.text: Apresoline is lisinopril, and -sartan drugs are ACE inhibitors ending in -pril.
choices.note: No. Lisinopril is Zestril, an ACE inhibitor; -sartan is the ARB suffix.

choices.text: Apresoline is verapamil, and losartan is a non-DHP calcium blocker.
choices.note: No. Verapamil is Isoptin, a non-DHP; losartan is listed with the ARBs.

choices.text: Both are selective alpha-1 blockers ending in -osin for BPH.
choices.note: No. The -osin alpha-1 blockers on this page are prazosin and terazosin.

choices.text: Apresoline is hydralazine, a hydrazinophthalazine vasodilator; -sartan drugs such as losartan, valsartan, candesartan, and irbesartan are ARBs that block angiotensin II, dilate vessels, and reduce aldosterone.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Apresoline (hydralazine) is a hydrazinophthalazine antihypertensive vasodilator, and ARBs ending in -sartan block angiotensin II, cause vasodilation, and reduce aldosterone.

scene: A nurse looks at Isordil, Elantan, and Angised on an antianginal chart.
ask: Which nitrate pairing does the note give?

choices.text: Isordil is glyceryl trinitrate, Elantan is dipyridamole, and Angised is digoxin.
choices.note: No. Dipyridamole is Persantin and digoxin is Lanoxin, not these nitrate brands.

choices.text: All three are beta blockers, and Elantan is metoprolol.
choices.note: No. Metoprolol is Betaloc, a beta blocker, not a nitrate brand.

choices.text: Isordil is isosorbide dinitrate, Elantan is isosorbide mononitrate, and Angised TNG is glyceryl trinitrate.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, these are antianginal nitrate vasodilators: Isordil (isosorbide dinitrate), Elantan (isosorbide mononitrate), and Angised TNG (glyceryl trinitrate).

choices.text: Isordil is amiodarone, Elantan is lignocaine, and Angised is phenytoin.
choices.note: No. Those three are antidysrhythmics (Cordarone, Xylocaine, and Dilantin), not nitrates.

scene: A nurse looks at Persantin on a chart beside antianginal medicines.
ask: What does the note call Persantin on this page?

choices.text: Digoxin, a cardiac glycoside that inhibits Na/K-ATPase.
choices.note: No. That mechanism belongs to Lanoxin (digoxin), not Persantin.

choices.text: Dipyridamole, listed as an antianginal antiplatelet.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Persantin is dipyridamole and is classed as antianginal and antiplatelet.

choices.text: Phenytoin, a hydantoin anticonvulsant and antidysrhythmic.
choices.note: No. Phenytoin is Dilantin in the antidysrhythmic list.

choices.text: Glyceryl trinitrate, a nitrate vasodilator.
choices.note: No. Glyceryl trinitrate is Angised TNG, a nitrate, not Persantin.

scene: A nurse looks at Lanoxin on a chart for atrial fibrillation and heart failure.
ask: What mechanism and uses does the note give Lanoxin?

choices.text: Digoxin inhibits Na/K-ATPase, raises calcium inside heart-muscle cells, and strengthens contraction; uses written are atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, and congestive heart failure.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Lanoxin (digoxin) inhibits Na/K-ATPase, increases intracellular calcium, and strengthens contraction for atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, and congestive heart failure.

choices.text: It is a class III antidysrhythmic and a noncompetitive alpha and beta antagonist.
choices.note: No. That class III line is written for Cordarone (amiodarone).

choices.text: It is a local anaesthetic antidysrhythmic also called lignocaine.
choices.note: No. Lignocaine/lidocaine is Xylocaine, not Lanoxin.

choices.text: It blocks angiotensin II binding and reduces aldosterone.
choices.note: No. That is the ARB mechanism on the antihypertensive page.

scene: A nurse looks at Cordarone, Xylocaine, and Dilantin on an antidysrhythmic chart.
ask: Which class line matches the note?

choices.text: Cordarone is digoxin, Xylocaine is verapamil, and Dilantin is diltiazem.
choices.note: No. Digoxin is Lanoxin; verapamil and diltiazem are the non-DHP calcium blockers Isoptin and Herbesser.

choices.text: All three are nitrate vasodilators.
choices.note: No. The nitrate brands on this page are Isordil, Elantan, and Angised.

choices.text: Cordarone is a -pine DHP calcium blocker and Dilantin is an ARB ending in -sartan.
choices.note: No. DHPs and ARBs are separate classes; these three names are antidysrhythmics.

choices.text: Cordarone is amiodarone, a class III antidysrhythmic; Xylocaine is lignocaine/lidocaine, a local anaesthetic and antidysrhythmic; Dilantin is phenytoin, a hydantoin anticonvulsant and antidysrhythmic.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, amiodarone is a class III antidysrhythmic and noncompetitive alpha and beta antagonist, lignocaine/lidocaine is a local anaesthetic antidysrhythmic, and phenytoin is the hydantoin antidysrhythmic.

scene: A nurse looks at Gelusil and Triact on a gastric chart.
ask: Which ingredients and roles does the note give these mixtures?

choices.text: Both are proton pump inhibitors ending in -zole.
choices.note: No. The -zole PPI brands on this page include Losec, Pariet, Pantaloc, Nexium, and Takepron.

choices.text: Both are H2 blockers, and simethicone is ranitidine.
choices.note: No. Ranitidine is Zantac, an H2-receptor antagonist ending in -dine.

choices.text: Both contain aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, and simethicone; aluminium hydroxide is an antacid, magnesium hydroxide is an antacid and laxative, and simethicone is an anti-flatulent.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Gelusil and Triact combine aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, and simethicone, with those antacid, laxative, and anti-flatulent roles.

choices.text: Gelusil is sucralfate and Triact is metoclopramide.
choices.note: No. Sucralfate is Carafate/Sulcrate, and metoclopramide is Maxolon.

scene: A nurse looks at Mucaine on a chart for stomach burning.
ask: What does the note say Mucaine contains, and for what symptom?

choices.text: It is rabeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor.
choices.note: No. Rabeprazole is Pariet, a PPI, not Mucaine.

choices.text: Aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, and oxethazaine, a local anaesthetic, for stomach pain and heartburn from too much acid.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Mucaine is an antacid with aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, and oxethazaine for 胃酸過多引起之胃痛及胃灼熱.

choices.text: It is sucralfate, listed only as an ulcer protectant.
choices.note: No. The protectant named here is Carafate/Sulcrate (sucralfate).

choices.text: It is bismuth subsalicylate for mild diarrhoea.
choices.note: No. Bismuth subsalicylate is the current identity of Kaopectate/Pepto-Bismol.

scene: A nurse looks at Pariet, Losec, Pantaloc, Nexium, and Takepron on an ulcer chart.
ask: Which proton pump inhibitor pairs match the note?

choices.text: Pariet is rabeprazole, Losec is omeprazole, Pantaloc is pantoprazole, Nexium is esomeprazole, and Takepron is lansoprazole.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, proton pump inhibitors end in -zole: Pariet (rabeprazole), Losec (omeprazole), Pantaloc (pantoprazole), Nexium (esomeprazole), and Takepron (lansoprazole).

choices.text: Pariet is cimetidine, Losec is famotidine, and Pantaloc is ranitidine.
choices.note: No. Cimetidine, famotidine, and ranitidine are the H2-receptor antagonists ending in -dine.

choices.text: All five end in -dine and are H2 blockers.
choices.note: No. The note groups these brands under proton pump inhibitors with the suffix -zole.

choices.text: Pariet is sucralfate, Nexium is loperamide, and Takepron is bisacodyl.
choices.note: No. Those are a protectant, an antidiarrhoeal, and a stimulant laxative, not this PPI list.

scene: A nurse looks at Tagamet, Pepcidine, and Zantac on an ulcer chart.
ask: Which duration and recall line matches the note?

choices.text: All three are proton pump inhibitors ending in -zole, and none is described as recalled.
choices.note: No. The -zole drugs are the PPI list; these -dine drugs are H2 blockers.

choices.text: Pepcidine is omeprazole and Tagamet is sucralfate.
choices.note: No. Omeprazole is Losec and sucralfate is Carafate/Sulcrate.

choices.text: Tagamet is long-acting and famotidine is the drug recalled for NDMA.
choices.note: No. The note calls cimetidine short-acting and ties the NDMA recall to original ranitidine.

choices.text: Tagamet (cimetidine) is short-acting, Pepcidine (famotidine) is long-acting, and original Zantac (ranitidine) was recalled because of NDMA carcinogen risk.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, cimetidine is short-acting, famotidine is long-acting, and original ranitidine (Zantac) was recalled for a carcinogen (NDMA).

scene: A nurse looks at Holopon and Maxolon on a nausea chart.
ask: How does the note separate these two antiemetic names?

choices.text: Both are stimulant laxatives, and Maxolon is senna.
choices.note: No. Senna is Senokot, a stimulant laxative, not metoclopramide.

choices.text: Holopon is prochlorperazine and Maxolon is promethazine.
choices.note: No. Prochlorperazine is Stemetil and promethazine is Phenergan/Phensedyl.

choices.text: Holopon/Buscopan is hyoscine butylbromide, an anticholinergic antispasmodic; Maxolon is metoclopramide, a dopaminergic blocker and GI stimulant.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Buscopan is hyoscine butylbromide (anticholinergic, antimuscarinic, antispasmodic) and Maxolon is metoclopramide, a dopaminergic blocker and GI stimulant.

choices.text: Holopon is sucralfate and Maxolon is omeprazole.
choices.note: No. Sucralfate is the ulcer protectant and omeprazole is Losec.

scene: A nurse looks at Stemetil and Phenergan on an antiemetic chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Stemetil is metoclopramide and Phenergan is hyoscine.
choices.note: No. Metoclopramide is Maxolon and hyoscine butylbromide is Buscopan.

choices.text: Stemetil is prochlorperazine, an antiemetic, antipsychotic, and dopaminergic blocker; Phenergan/Phensedyl is promethazine, an H1 antihistamine, antiemetic, and phenothiazine.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Stemetil is prochlorperazine maleate and Phenergan is promethazine HCl, both with antiemetic and dopaminergic-blocker lines.

choices.text: Both are proton pump inhibitors ending in -zole.
choices.note: No. The -zole antiulcer drugs are a different GI group.

choices.text: Stemetil is loperamide and Phenergan is lactulose.
choices.note: No. Loperamide is Imodium and lactulose is Duphalac.

scene: A nurse looks at Dulcolax, Duphalac, Metamucil, and Senokot on a bowel chart.
ask: Which laxative classes match the note?

choices.text: Dulcolax (bisacodyl) and Senokot (senna) are stimulant laxatives; Duphalac (lactulose) is hyperosmotic and an ammonia detoxicant; Metamucil (psyllium) is bulk-forming.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, bisacodyl and senna are stimulant laxatives, lactulose is a hyperosmotic laxative and ammonia detoxicant, and psyllium is bulk-forming.

choices.text: All four are opioid antidiarrhoeals.
choices.note: No. The antidiarrhoeals named nearby are loperamide, diphenoxylate with atropine, and bismuth subsalicylate.

choices.text: Lactulose is bulk-forming fibre and psyllium is the ammonia detoxicant.
choices.note: No. The note gives bulk-forming to psyllium and the ammonia-detoxicant line to lactulose.

choices.text: Bisacodyl is bismuth subsalicylate and senna is loperamide.
choices.note: No. Bismuth is Kaopectate/Pepto-Bismol and loperamide is Imodium.

scene: A nurse looks at Imodium, Lomotil, and Kaopectate on a diarrhoea chart.
ask: Which identities match the note?

choices.text: Imodium is senna, Lomotil is lactulose, and Kaopectate is psyllium.
choices.note: No. Senna, lactulose, and psyllium are the laxatives, not these antidiarrhoeals.

choices.text: All three are proton pump inhibitors ending in -zole.
choices.note: No. PPIs are the -zole antiulcer group.

choices.text: Kaopectate is still written as a kaolin-pectin mixture, and Imodium is sucralfate.
choices.note: No. The note says Kaopectate is no longer kaolin-pectin, and sucralfate is Carafate.

choices.text: Imodium is loperamide; Lomotil is diphenoxylate with atropine; Kaopectate, also named Pepto-Bismol, is now bismuth subsalicylate and is no longer a kaolin-pectin mixture.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Imodium is loperamide, Lomotil is diphenoxylate with atropine, and Kaopectate/Pepto-Bismol is bismuth subsalicylate, not the old kaolin-pectin mix.

scene: A nurse looks at Essentiale, Anusol, Faktu, and Carafate on a GI chart.
ask: Which roles match the note?

choices.text: All four are stimulant laxatives.
choices.note: No. Stimulant laxatives in this section are bisacodyl and senna.

choices.text: Essentiale is loperamide, Anusol is omeprazole, and Carafate is senna.
choices.note: No. Loperamide, omeprazole, and senna are different GI drugs in the note.

choices.text: Essentiale (polyenylphosphatidylcholine) is a hepatic protector; Anusol and Faktu are anorectal preparations; Carafate/Sulcrate is sucralfate, an ulcer protectant.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Essentiale is PPC for liver protection, Anusol (zinc oxide, benzyl benzoate) and Faktu (policresulen, cinchocaine) are anorectal preparations, and Carafate/Sulcrate is sucralfate.

choices.text: Carafate is bismuth subsalicylate and Essentiale is a proton pump inhibitor.
choices.note: No. Bismuth is Kaopectate/Pepto-Bismol, and PPIs are the separate -zole list.

scene: A nurse looks at the comparison table for Metamucil and Duphalac.
ask: How does that table contrast psyllium and lactulose?

choices.text: Both are stimulant laxatives with onset in 15 to 60 minutes.
choices.note: No. The 15-60 minute line is the bisacodyl suppository, and these two are not both stimulants.

choices.text: Psyllium is a water-soluble fibre that forms a gel and increases stool bulk, with onset about 12 to 72 hours; lactulose is an osmotic laxative for constipation and hepatic encephalopathy, with onset about 24 to 48 hours.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, psyllium absorbs water to form a gel and increase stool volume over 12-72 hours, while lactulose draws water into the bowel and is also written to reduce ammonia absorption in hepatic encephalopathy.

choices.text: Lactulose is the bulk-forming fibre and psyllium is the drug written for hepatic encephalopathy.
choices.note: No. The table gives hepatic encephalopathy to lactulose and the gel-forming fibre line to psyllium.

choices.text: Psyllium onset is 6 to 12 hours and the table lists galactosaemia under psyllium.
choices.note: No. The 6-12 hour oral onset and the galactosaemia line are written with the other laxatives, not as the psyllium onset.

scene: A nurse looks at bisacodyl and senna on a pre-procedure bowel chart.
ask: What type and timing does the table give these two laxatives?

choices.text: Both are stimulant laxatives for constipation and bowel emptying; oral onset is about 6 to 12 hours, bisacodyl suppositories are 15 to 60 minutes, and continuous use beyond 7 days is not advised.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, bisacodyl and senna are stimulant laxatives, oral onset is 6-12 hours, a bisacodyl suppository is 15-60 minutes, and use is short-term, not more than 7 days in a row.

choices.text: Both are bulk-forming fibres that the table calls safe for daily long-term use.
choices.note: No. Daily long-term use is the psyllium column, not the stimulant columns.

choices.text: Senna is osmotic and is the laxative written for hepatic encephalopathy.
choices.note: No. The osmotic laxative for hepatic encephalopathy in the table is lactulose.

choices.text: Bisacodyl is an antidiarrhoeal that slows the gut, like loperamide.
choices.note: No. Loperamide is Imodium, an antidiarrhoeal, not the stimulant bisacodyl.

scene: A nurse looks at Atrovent and Spiriva on a respiratory chart.
ask: How does the note distinguish these anticholinergic bronchodilators?

choices.text: Both are short-acting beta-2 agonists, and Spiriva is salbutamol.
choices.note: No. Salbutamol is Ventolin, a short-acting beta-2 agonist, not tiotropium.

choices.text: Atrovent is an inhaled corticosteroid and Spiriva is theophylline.
choices.note: No. Inhaled corticosteroids here include beclomethasone and budesonide; theophylline is Theodur/Nuelin.

choices.text: Spiriva is the short-acting agent and Atrovent is the 24-hour drug.
choices.note: No. The note calls ipratropium short-acting and tiotropium the long-acting 24-hour drug.

choices.text: Atrovent is ipratropium, a short-acting muscarinic antagonist; Spiriva is tiotropium, a long-acting muscarinic antagonist written as bronchodilating for 24 hours.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, ipratropium is a SAMA that blocks M3 receptors, and tiotropium is a LAMA with bronchodilation lasting 24 hours.

scene: A nurse looks at Ventolin, Xopenex, and Bricanyl on an asthma chart.
ask: Which description matches the note?

choices.text: They are long-acting muscarinic antagonists.
choices.note: No. The long-acting muscarinic antagonist in this section is tiotropium (Spiriva).

choices.text: Ventolin is ipratropium, Xopenex is fluticasone, and Bricanyl is budesonide.
choices.note: No. Ipratropium is Atrovent, and fluticasone and budesonide are corticosteroid names here.

choices.text: All three are short-acting beta-2 agonists: Ventolin is salbutamol, Xopenex is levosalbutamol, and Bricanyl is terbutaline, also written as a tocolytic.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Ventolin, Xopenex, and Bricanyl are SABAs; Xopenex is said to have fewer cardiac effects, Ventolin is mainly for acute attacks, and terbutaline is also a tocolytic (子宮抑制劑) written as suiting longer maintenance.

choices.text: Bricanyl is a xanthine that inhibits phosphodiesterase.
choices.note: No. The xanthine PDE inhibitor in the note is theophylline.

scene: A nurse looks at Seretide, Becloforte, and Pulmicort on an inhaler chart.
ask: What does the note say these inhalers contain?

choices.text: Becloforte is tiotropium and Pulmicort is salbutamol.
choices.note: No. Tiotropium is Spiriva and salbutamol is Ventolin.

choices.text: Seretide is salmeterol (Serevent), a LABA, plus fluticasone; Becloforte/Beclovent is beclomethasone and Pulmicort is budesonide, both inhaled corticosteroids.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Seretide combines the LABA salmeterol with fluticasone, and beclomethasone and budesonide are inhaled glucocorticoids.

choices.text: All three are xanthines that inhibit phosphodiesterase.
choices.note: No. The xanthine bronchodilator named here is theophylline.

choices.text: Seretide is ipratropium plus theophylline.
choices.note: No. Ipratropium is Atrovent and theophylline is Theodur/Nuelin, not the Seretide pair.

scene: A nurse looks at Theodur on a chart for wheeze.
ask: What class and mechanism does the note give theophylline?

choices.text: Theodur/Nuelin SR is theophylline, a xanthine bronchodilator and spasmolytic that inhibits phosphodiesterase.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, theophylline is a xanthine (黃嘌呤類) and PDE inhibitor used as a bronchodilator for asthma, COPD, and bronchospasm.

choices.text: It is a long-acting muscarinic antagonist that blocks M3 receptors for 24 hours.
choices.note: No. That 24-hour M3 block is the tiotropium line.

choices.text: It is an inhaled glucocorticoid like budesonide.
choices.note: No. Budesonide is Pulmicort, an inhaled corticosteroid.

choices.text: It is a short-acting beta-2 agonist like salbutamol.
choices.note: No. Salbutamol is Ventolin, a SABA, not the xanthine.

scene: A nurse looks at a corticosteroid teaching note beside prednisolone.
ask: Which effects does this respiratory page list for corticosteroids?

choices.text: They are written only as mucolytics that break mucus polysaccharides.
choices.note: No. Breaking mucus polysaccharides is the bromhexine line on this page.

choices.text: They block M3 receptors and are called SAMA drugs.
choices.note: No. SAMA is the ipratropium description.

choices.text: They are opioid antitussives acting on the cough centre.
choices.note: No. The opioid cough drug in the next pages is codeine; dextromethorphan is the non-opioid.

choices.text: Adrenal suppression through the HPA axis, osteoporosis, slowed growth in children, and glaucoma or cataract.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, corticosteroids can suppress the HPA axis, weaken bone, slow growth in children, and raise the chance of glaucoma and cataract.

scene: A nurse looks at Bisolvon and Fluimucil on a cough chart.
ask: What does the note say these two do?

choices.text: Both are opioid antitussives, and Fluimucil is codeine.
choices.note: No. Codeine is the opioid antitussive; Fluimucil is N-acetylcysteine.

choices.text: Bisolvon is salbutamol and Fluimucil is ipratropium.
choices.note: No. Salbutamol and ipratropium are bronchodilators, not these mucolytic names.

choices.text: Bisolvon is bromhexine, a mucolytic for sputum that is hard to clear; Fluimucil is N-acetylcysteine, written for thick sputum and as a paracetamol-overdose antidote.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, bromhexine is a mucolytic, and NAC (Fluimucil) is both a mucolytic and a paracetamol-overdose antidote.

choices.text: Fluimucil is only a nasal decongestant and has no antidote line.
choices.note: No. The nasal decongestant in the Actifed note is pseudoephedrine; NAC has an antidote line.

scene: A nurse looks at MES and Actifed compound on a cold-symptom chart.
ask: Which component roles match the note?

choices.text: MES is codeine and Actifed is a LABA plus steroid inhaler.
choices.note: No. Codeine is a separate opioid antitussive, and the LABA-steroid inhaler is Seretide.

choices.text: MES is an expectorant stimulant with ammonia carbonate and ipecacuanha; Actifed compound pairs dextromethorphan, pseudoephedrine, and triprolidine.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, MES stimulates cough or secretions, and Actifed compound is dextromethorphan (non-opioid antitussive), pseudoephedrine (nasal decongestant), and triprolidine (antihistamine).

choices.text: Dextromethorphan is an opioid, and pseudoephedrine is a mucolytic like bromhexine.
choices.note: No. The note calls dextromethorphan a non-opioid antitussive and pseudoephedrine a decongestant.

choices.text: Triprolidine is a xanthine PDE inhibitor.
choices.note: No. The xanthine PDE inhibitor is theophylline, not triprolidine.

scene: A nurse looks at dextromethorphan on a non-opioid cough chart.
ask: How does the note describe its mechanism?

choices.text: A non-opioid antitussive that suppresses the medullary cough centre and reduces the cough reflex.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, dextromethorphan suppresses the medullary cough centre (延腦咳嗽中樞) and is not classed as an opioid antitussive.

choices.text: It binds opioid receptors and is the opioid antitussive codeine.
choices.note: No. Codeine is the opioid antitussive; dextromethorphan is the non-opioid.

choices.text: It blocks pulmonary M3 receptors like ipratropium.
choices.note: No. M3 blockade is the anticholinergic bronchodilator mechanism.

choices.text: It inhibits phosphodiesterase like theophylline.
choices.note: No. Phosphodiesterase inhibition is the theophylline line.

scene: A nurse looks at codeine phosphate on a cough chart.
ask: What class and mechanism does the note give codeine?

choices.text: A non-opioid antitussive that only suppresses cough and has no analgesic line.
choices.note: No. That non-opioid cough description is dextromethorphan.

choices.text: A first-generation antihistamine used for motion sickness.
choices.note: No. Motion sickness in this section is written for diphenhydramine (Benadryl).

choices.text: A short-acting beta-2 agonist also called terbutaline.
choices.note: No. Terbutaline is Bricanyl, a SABA, not codeine.

choices.text: An opioid antitussive and analgesic that acts on the central cough centre and on opioid receptors.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, codeine phosphate is an opioid antitussive and analgesic acting on the central cough centre and on opioid receptors.

scene: A nurse looks at Ascopine on a cough-and-cold chart.
ask: Which ingredients does the note list in Ascopine?

choices.text: Dextromethorphan, pseudoephedrine, and triprolidine only.
choices.note: No. That trio is Actifed compound, not Ascopine.

choices.text: Salbutamol, ipratropium, and budesonide.
choices.note: No. Those are bronchodilator and corticosteroid inhaler drugs, not Ascopine.

choices.text: Codeine, Piriton (chlorpheniramine), caffeine anhydrous, and DL-methylephedrine.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Ascopine contains codeine, chlorpheniramine (Piriton), anhydrous caffeine, and DL-methylephedrine for coughs and cold symptoms.

choices.text: Bromhexine and N-acetylcysteine only.
choices.note: No. Those are the mucolytics Bisolvon and Fluimucil.

scene: A nurse looks at Benadryl on an allergy and sleep chart.
ask: What does the note say diphenhydramine does?

choices.text: It is a second-generation antihistamine with no sedation line.
choices.note: No. The note puts diphenhydramine with first-generation H1 blockade and sedation.

choices.text: Benadryl is diphenhydramine, a first-generation antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors, has anticholinergic effects, and is written for allergy, motion sickness, and sleep.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, diphenhydramine blocks H1 receptors, has anticholinergic effects, and is used for allergy, motion sickness, and short-term sleep.

choices.text: It is an opioid antitussive like codeine.
choices.note: No. Codeine is the opioid cough and pain drug; Benadryl is the antihistamine.

choices.text: It is a nasal decongestant that constricts nasal vessels, like pseudoephedrine.
choices.note: No. Pseudoephedrine is the decongestant in Actifed; Benadryl is diphenhydramine.

scene: A nurse looks at a seizure chart that names hydantoins and succinimides.
ask: How does the note match these groups to seizure types?

choices.text: Hydantoins are for generalized tonic-clonic seizures, status epilepticus, and psychomotor seizures; succinimides are for absence seizures.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, hydantoins inhibit spread of seizure activity in the motor cortex for those major seizures, while succinimides inhibit spike-and-wave formation for absence seizures.

choices.text: Succinimides are for status epilepticus and hydantoins are only for absence seizures.
choices.note: No. The note gives absence seizures to succinimides and status epilepticus to hydantoins.

choices.text: Both groups are benzodiazepines used only for alcohol withdrawal.
choices.note: No. Alcohol-withdrawal use is written later with benzodiazepines such as diazepam.

choices.text: Hydantoins enhance GABA and are the barbiturate phenobarbital.
choices.note: No. Enhancing GABA and prolonging chloride-channel opening is the phenobarbital line.

scene: A nurse looks at Epilim, Dilantin, and Tegretol on a seizure chart.
ask: Which brand-generic pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Epilim is phenytoin, Dilantin is diazepam, and Tegretol is lorazepam.
choices.note: No. Diazepam is Valium and lorazepam is Ativan; Dilantin is phenytoin.

choices.text: Epilim is ethosuximide, Dilantin is phenobarbital, and Tegretol is valproate.
choices.note: No. Ethosuximide and phenobarbital appear as class examples, but these brands are valproate, phenytoin, and carbamazepine.

choices.text: All three are benzodiazepines, and Tegretol is lorazepam.
choices.note: No. The benzodiazepines named are diazepam and lorazepam, not this trio.

choices.text: Epilim is valproate, Dilantin is phenytoin, and Tegretol is carbamazepine.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Epilim is valproate, Dilantin is phenytoin (a hydantoin), and Tegretol is carbamazepine.

scene: A nurse looks at Tegretol beside a note about face pain and mood.
ask: Which uses does the note write for carbamazepine?

choices.text: Only absence seizures, as a succinimide.
choices.note: No. Absence seizures are the succinimide use; ethosuximide is the example.

choices.text: Parkinsonism and restless legs syndrome.
choices.note: No. Those uses are written for Sinemet, the carbidopa-levodopa product.

choices.text: Tonic-clonic, complex-partial, and mixed seizures, plus trigeminal neuralgia and bipolar disorder.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Tegretol (carbamazepine) is for tonic-clonic, complex-partial, and mixed seizures, trigeminal neuralgia, and bipolar disorder.

choices.text: Asthma and COPD as a bronchodilator.
choices.note: No. Asthma and COPD bronchodilation is the respiratory section, not carbamazepine.

scene: A nurse looks at Valium and Ativan on a neurologic chart.
ask: What class does the note give these two?

choices.text: Valium is phenytoin and Ativan is carbamazepine, both hydantoins.
choices.note: No. Phenytoin is Dilantin and carbamazepine is Tegretol.

choices.text: Both are benzodiazepines; Valium is diazepam and Ativan is lorazepam, and both have anticonvulsant lines.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Valium is diazepam and Ativan is lorazepam, benzodiazepines with anxiolytic and anticonvulsant actions.

choices.text: Both are barbiturates, and Ativan is phenobarbital.
choices.note: No. Phenobarbital is the barbiturate example; Ativan is lorazepam.

choices.text: Valium is valproate and Ativan is ethosuximide.
choices.note: No. Valproate is Epilim and ethosuximide is the succinimide example.

scene: A nurse looks at a benzodiazepine mechanism line beside diazepam.
ask: What mechanism does the note give benzodiazepines?

choices.text: They promote GABA binding at the GABA-A receptor, increase chloride inflow, and strengthen inhibitory transmission.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, benzodiazepines such as diazepam and lorazepam promote GABA binding at GABA-A receptors and increase chloride influx.

choices.text: They block voltage-dependent sodium channels the way the note describes carbamazepine.
choices.note: No. Voltage-dependent sodium-channel blockade is the carbamazepine line.

choices.text: They inhibit T-type calcium channels the way the note describes ethosuximide.
choices.note: No. T-type calcium-channel inhibition is the succinimide (ethosuximide) line.

choices.text: They inhibit peripheral DOPA decarboxylase the way the note describes carbidopa.
choices.note: No. Peripheral DOPA decarboxylase inhibition is the carbidopa part of Sinemet.

scene: A nurse looks at Epilim and Tegretol mechanism lines.
ask: Which mechanism summary matches the note?

choices.text: Valproate is an anticholinergic and carbamazepine is levodopa.
choices.note: No. The anticholinergic is trihexyphenidyl and levodopa is part of Sinemet.

choices.text: Both only inhibit spike-and-wave discharges as succinimides.
choices.note: No. Spike-and-wave inhibition is the succinimide description.

choices.text: Carbamazepine inhibits Na/K-ATPase like digoxin.
choices.note: No. Na/K-ATPase inhibition is the digoxin mechanism.

choices.text: Valproate blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels and T-type calcium channels and increases GABA effect; carbamazepine blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Epilim (valproate) affects sodium channels, T-type calcium channels, and GABA, while Tegretol (carbamazepine) blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels.

scene: A nurse looks at Artane on a Parkinson chart.
ask: What is Artane, and what balance does the note say it restores?

choices.text: Artane is carbidopa-levodopa, a dopamine precursor combination.
choices.note: No. Carbidopa with levodopa is Sinemet, not Artane.

choices.text: Artane is haloperidol, a dopamine D2 blocker.
choices.note: No. Haloperidol is Haldol, a typical antipsychotic, not the anticholinergic.

choices.text: Artane is trihexyphenidyl, an anticholinergic that inhibits acetylcholine and restores dopamine-acetylcholine balance, reducing tremor and rigidity.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, trihexyphenidyl blocks acetylcholine and restores dopamine-acetylcholine balance for parkinsonian symptoms and drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms.

choices.text: Artane is phenytoin, a hydantoin anticonvulsant.
choices.note: No. Phenytoin is Dilantin, a hydantoin, not trihexyphenidyl.

scene: A nurse looks at Sinemet 25/100 on a Parkinson chart.
ask: How does the note explain the two parts of Sinemet?

choices.text: Carbidopa becomes dopamine in the brain and levodopa only blocks acetylcholine.
choices.note: No. The note says levodopa becomes dopamine and carbidopa blocks peripheral decarboxylase.

choices.text: Levodopa is a dopamine precursor that crosses into the brain and becomes dopamine; carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase so more levodopa enters the brain.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Sinemet is carbidopa plus levodopa; carbidopa blocks peripheral decarboxylase and levodopa becomes dopamine in the brain.

choices.text: Sinemet is trihexyphenidyl, an anticholinergic only.
choices.note: No. Trihexyphenidyl is Artane; Sinemet is the dopamine-precursor combination.

choices.text: Both drugs block D2 receptors like an antipsychotic.
choices.note: No. D2 blockade is the haloperidol line, not Sinemet.

scene: A nurse looks at an insulin order beside notes on oral antidiabetics.
ask: Which insulin lines match the note?

choices.text: Insulin is for ketoacidosis and type 1 and type 2 diabetes; warm it in the palms so cold insulin does not cause lipodystrophy, and rotate sites.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, insulin is for ketoacidosis and type 1 and 2 diabetes, should be warmed by rotating in the palms, and sites include abdomen, upper back, thighs, upper arm, and buttocks. Oral antidiabetics are written for type 2 diabetes.

choices.text: Oral sulfonylureas are written as the first choice for type 1 diabetes.
choices.note: No. The note says sulfonylureas are not for loss of islet function in type 1 diabetes.

choices.text: Insulin is only a biguanide taken by mouth.
choices.note: No. The biguanide taken by mouth is metformin (Glucophage).

choices.text: Insulin and the oral agents are both SGLT-2 inhibitors.
choices.note: No. SGLT-2 inhibitors in the note are drugs such as dapagliflozin and empagliflozin.

scene: A nurse looks at Daonil, Diamicron, and Tol-Tab on a diabetes chart.
ask: What class and generics does the note give?

choices.text: They are biguanides, and Daonil is metformin.
choices.note: No. Metformin is Glucophage, the biguanide, not Daonil.

choices.text: They are alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, and Diamicron is acarbose.
choices.note: No. Acarbose is Glucobay, the alpha-glucosidase inhibitor.

choices.text: They are SGLT-2 inhibitors, and Tol-Tab is dapagliflozin.
choices.note: No. Dapagliflozin is Forxiga, an SGLT-2 inhibitor.

choices.text: They are sulfonylurea hypoglycaemics: Daonil is glibenclamide, Diamicron is gliclazide, and Tol-Tab is tolbutamide, stimulating beta cells to release insulin.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, glibenclamide, gliclazide, and tolbutamide are sulfonylureas that stimulate pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion for type 2 diabetes.

scene: A nurse looks at Glucophage and Glucobay on a type 2 diabetes chart.
ask: How does the note separate their mechanisms?

choices.text: Glucophage blocks SGLT-2 in the kidney and Glucobay is insulin.
choices.note: No. SGLT-2 blockade is dapagliflozin or empagliflozin, not metformin.

choices.text: Both stimulate beta cells the way sulfonylureas do.
choices.note: No. Stimulating beta cells is the sulfonylurea mechanism, not these two.

choices.text: Glucophage is metformin, a biguanide that suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis, reduces intestinal glucose absorption, and increases insulin sensitivity; Glucobay is acarbose, which slows carbohydrate breakdown.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, metformin works on liver glucose output, gut absorption, and insulin sensitivity, while acarbose slows carbohydrate digestion at the intestinal lining.

choices.text: Glucobay is sitagliptin and Glucophage is pioglitazone.
choices.note: No. Sitagliptin is Januvia, a DPP-4 inhibitor, and pioglitazone is Actos, a TZD.

topic: DPP-4 inhibitor, SGLT-2 inhibitor, and TZD
scene: A nurse looks at Januvia, Forxiga, and Actos on a diabetes chart.
ask: Which class pairing matches the note?

choices.text: All three are sulfonylureas, and Forxiga is glibenclamide.
choices.note: No. Glibenclamide is Daonil, a sulfonylurea, not dapagliflozin.

choices.text: Januvia (sitagliptin) is a DPP-4 inhibitor, Forxiga (dapagliflozin) is an SGLT-2 inhibitor, and Actos (pioglitazone) is a thiazolidinedione.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, sitagliptin inhibits DPP-4, dapagliflozin inhibits SGLT-2 so glucose leaves in urine, and pioglitazone is a TZD that activates PPAR-gamma.

choices.text: Januvia is metformin, Forxiga is acarbose, and Actos is tolbutamide.
choices.note: No. Those generics belong to Glucophage, Glucobay, and Tol-Tab.

choices.text: Actos is empagliflozin and Forxiga is linagliptin.
choices.note: No. Empagliflozin is Jardiance, an SGLT-2 inhibitor, and linagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor.

scene: A nurse looks at generation notes for Daonil and tolbutamide.
ask: How does the comparison table class these sulfonylureas?

choices.text: Daonil (glibenclamide) and Diamicron (gliclazide) are second-generation; tolbutamide is first-generation and shorter-acting than glibenclamide.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, glibenclamide and gliclazide are second-generation sulfonylureas and tolbutamide is first-generation with a shorter action than glibenclamide.

choices.text: Tolbutamide is a biguanide and glibenclamide is an SGLT-2 inhibitor.
choices.note: No. The biguanide is metformin and the SGLT-2 examples are dapagliflozin and empagliflozin.

choices.text: All three are alpha-glucosidase inhibitors.
choices.note: No. The alpha-glucosidase inhibitor in the table is acarbose.

choices.text: Gliclazide is first-generation and tolbutamide is a thiazolidinedione.
choices.note: No. The note calls gliclazide second-generation; TZDs are pioglitazone and rosiglitazone.

scene: A nurse looks at Diamicron on a chart that also mentions clotting and oxidation.
ask: Besides lowering glucose, what extra actions does the note give gliclazide?

choices.text: It inhibits SGLT-2 and causes glucose to leave in the urine.
choices.note: No. Urinary glucose loss is the SGLT-2 inhibitor mechanism.

choices.text: It is only an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor taken with the first bite of a meal.
choices.note: No. The first-bite instruction is written for acarbose (Glucobay).

choices.text: It blocks DPP-4 and is the generic sitagliptin.
choices.note: No. Sitagliptin is Januvia, a DPP-4 inhibitor.

choices.text: Fibrinolytic, antioxidant, and antiplatelet actions.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Diamicron (gliclazide) is a sulfonylurea with fibrinolytic, antioxidant, and antiplatelet actions.

scene: A nurse looks at a hypoglycaemia note under Glucobay.
ask: If hypoglycaemia occurs with acarbose, what does the note say to give?

choices.text: Sucrose, because the note says acarbose speeds sucrose absorption.
choices.note: No. The note says absorption is delayed, so sucrose is not the rescue sugar.

choices.text: A sulfonylurea, because acarbose is itself a sulfonylurea.
choices.note: No. Acarbose is the alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, not a sulfonylurea.

choices.text: Glucose, not sucrose, because acarbose delays sucrose absorption.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Glucobay (acarbose) delays carbohydrate absorption, so hypoglycaemia is treated with glucose rather than sucrose.

choices.text: Insulin, because the note classes acarbose as a biguanide.
choices.note: No. The biguanide is metformin; acarbose is Glucobay.

scene: A nurse looks at Lasix on a chart for pulmonary oedema.
ask: What is Lasix, and where does the note say loop diuretics act?

choices.text: Lasix is spironolactone, a potassium-sparing aldosterone antagonist.
choices.note: No. Spironolactone is Aldactone, the potassium-sparing diuretic.

choices.text: Lasix is furosemide, a loop diuretic on the thick ascending limb that inhibits the Na-K-2Cl transporter.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, furosemide (also written frusemide) inhibits Na-K-2Cl transport on the thick ascending limb; bumetanide is the other loop diuretic named.

choices.text: Lasix is indapamide, acting only on the distal convoluted tubule.
choices.note: No. Indapamide is Natrilix, a thiazide-like diuretic.

choices.text: Lasix is mannitol, an osmotic diuretic.
choices.note: No. Mannitol is the osmotic diuretic, not Lasix.

scene: A nurse looks at Natrilix and Diulo on a blood-pressure chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Natrilix is indapamide and Diulo is metolazone; both are thiazide-like diuretics inhibiting Na/Cl reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, indapamide and metolazone are thiazide-like diuretics, grouped with hydrochlorothiazide at the distal convoluted tubule.

choices.text: Both are loop diuretics, and Diulo is bumetanide.
choices.note: No. Bumetanide is listed with loop diuretics beside furosemide.

choices.text: Natrilix is acetazolamide and Diulo is mannitol.
choices.note: No. Acetazolamide is the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor and mannitol is osmotic.

choices.text: Both are potassium-sparing drugs, and Natrilix is amiloride.
choices.note: No. Amiloride is a potassium-sparing example; Natrilix is indapamide.

scene: A nurse looks at Aldactone on a heart-failure chart.
ask: What class and potassium effect does the note give Aldactone?

choices.text: It is a loop diuretic whose main electrolyte line is low potassium.
choices.note: No. Low potassium is a loop and thiazide problem in the note; spironolactone spares potassium.

choices.text: It is hydrochlorothiazide and has no aldosterone line.
choices.note: No. Hydrochlorothiazide is the thiazide example acting on Na/Cl reabsorption.

choices.text: It is acetazolamide, used for glaucoma and altitude sickness.
choices.note: No. Glaucoma and altitude sickness are acetazolamide uses.

choices.text: Aldactone is spironolactone, an aldosterone antagonist that lets sodium leave while potassium is kept.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, spironolactone antagonises aldosterone, wastes sodium, and spares potassium for heart-failure oedema, hypertension, and high aldosterone states.

scene: A nurse looks at mannitol on a chart for acute brain swelling.
ask: What class and action does the note give mannitol?

choices.text: A potassium-sparing aldosterone antagonist for cirrhotic ascites.
choices.note: No. Aldosterone antagonism and cirrhotic ascites are the spironolactone lines.

choices.text: A loop diuretic identical to furosemide.
choices.note: No. Furosemide is Lasix, the loop diuretic, not mannitol.

choices.text: An osmotic diuretic that holds water in the tubule, written for acute cerebral oedema, raised intracranial pressure, acute glaucoma, and promoting urine in acute renal failure.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, mannitol is an osmotic diuretic for acute cerebral oedema, intracranial hypertension, acute glaucoma, and the oliguric phase of acute renal failure.

choices.text: A carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used only for altitude sickness.
choices.note: No. Altitude sickness is an acetazolamide use.

scene: A nurse looks at acetazolamide on an eye-pressure chart.
ask: What mechanism and uses does the note give?

choices.text: It blocks the Na-K-2Cl transporter in the loop of Henle.
choices.note: No. Na-K-2Cl blockade is the loop-diuretic mechanism of furosemide.

choices.text: It inhibits carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule, reduces bicarbonate and sodium reabsorption, and is written for glaucoma, altitude sickness, and metabolic alkalosis.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor for glaucoma, altitude sickness, and metabolic alkalosis.

choices.text: It is an osmotic diuretic given for acute cerebral oedema.
choices.note: No. Acute cerebral oedema is a mannitol use.

choices.text: It is indapamide, a thiazide-like antihypertensive.
choices.note: No. Indapamide is Natrilix, a thiazide-like diuretic.

scene: A nurse looks at Diulo written next to Lasix.
ask: What does the note say about using metolazone with a loop diuretic?

choices.text: Metolazone inhibits Na/Cl reabsorption in the distal tubule, and combining it with a loop diuretic can strengthen the diuretic effect.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, metolazone (Diulo) is thiazide-like and can increase diuresis when combined with a loop diuretic.

choices.text: Metolazone is potassium-sparing and cancels the effect of furosemide.
choices.note: No. Potassium-sparing drugs in the note include spironolactone, amiloride, and triamterene, not metolazone.

choices.text: The combination is described as two carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
choices.note: No. Carbonic anhydrase inhibition is the acetazolamide mechanism.

choices.text: Diulo is mannitol and is not paired with Lasix in the note.
choices.note: No. The note does pair metolazone (Diulo) with loop diuretics such as Lasix.

scene: A nurse looks at Panadol, Voltaren, and Brufen on a pain chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Panadol is morphine, Voltaren is tramadol, and Brufen is pethidine.
choices.note: No. Morphine, tramadol (Ultram), and pethidine are opioid or central analgesics, not these brands.

choices.text: All three are opioid agonists acting on mu receptors.
choices.note: No. Mu-receptor agonism is the opioid analgesic line, not paracetamol or these NSAID brands.

choices.text: Voltaren is phenazopyridine and Brufen is dextropropoxyphene.
choices.note: No. Phenazopyridine is Pyridium and dextropropoxyphene is Doloxene.

choices.text: Panadol is paracetamol, an analgesic and antipyretic; Voltaren is diclofenac, an NSAID; Brufen is ibuprofen, an NSAID.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Panadol is paracetamol (acetaminophen), Voltaren is diclofenac sodium, and Brufen is ibuprofen.

scene: A nurse looks at Aspirin and Indocid on a pain-and-inflammation chart.
ask: What extra uses does the note attach to these two?

choices.text: Both are opioid agonists for severe postoperative pain only.
choices.note: No. Severe postoperative pain is written with opioids such as morphine and dihydrocodeine.

choices.text: Aspirin is paracetamol and the note gives paracetamol a strong anti-inflammatory action.
choices.note: No. Paracetamol is Panadol; a later line says paracetamol has no anti-inflammatory action.

choices.text: Aspirin is written for pain, inflammation, fever, and prevention of myocardial infarction, TIA, and thrombosis; Indocid (indomethacin) is also written for gout and a patent ductus arteriosus.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, aspirin has analgesic, antirheumatic, antipyretic, antiplatelet, and NSAID lines, and indomethacin is written for gout pain and patent ductus arteriosus.

choices.text: Indocid is naproxen and aspirin is mefenamic acid.
choices.note: No. Naproxen is Naprosyn and mefenamic acid is Ponstan/Hostan.

scene: A nurse looks at DF118, Ultram, and morphine on a severe-pain chart.
ask: Which identities match the note?

choices.text: All three are NSAIDs that only inhibit prostaglandin synthesis.
choices.note: No. Prostaglandin inhibition is the non-opioid/NSAID line; these names are in the opioid group.

choices.text: DF118 is dihydrocodeine, a synthetic opioid analgesic and antitussive; Ultram is tramadol, a central analgesic; morphine is an opioid agonist.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, dihydrocodeine, tramadol, and morphine are opioid or central analgesics, with morphine written for severe pain including around myocardial infarction.

choices.text: DF118 is ibuprofen, Ultram is aspirin, and morphine is paracetamol.
choices.note: No. Ibuprofen is Brufen, aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, and paracetamol is Panadol.

choices.text: Ultram is phenazopyridine, a urinary local analgesic.
choices.note: No. Phenazopyridine is Pyridium, a local analgesic excreted in urine.

scene: A nurse looks at Doloxene, Naprosyn, Ponstan, and Pyridium on a pain chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Doloxene is dextropropoxyphene; Naprosyn is naproxen; Ponstan/Hostan is mefenamic acid; Pyridium is phenazopyridine, a local analgesic excreted in urine.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Doloxene is dextropropoxyphene, Naprosyn is naproxen, Ponstan is mefenamic acid, and Pyridium is phenazopyridine for urinary-tract pain.

choices.text: All four are strong mu agonists like morphine.
choices.note: No. Morphine is the strong opioid agonist; naproxen and mefenamic acid are NSAIDs.

choices.text: Pyridium is diclofenac and Ponstan is codeine.
choices.note: No. Diclofenac is Voltaren and codeine is a separate opioid antitussive and analgesic.

choices.text: Naprosyn is paracetamol and Doloxene is ibuprofen.
choices.note: No. Paracetamol is Panadol and ibuprofen is Brufen.

scene: A nurse looks at a mechanism line under Panadol.
ask: How does the note describe paracetamol compared with an anti-inflammatory effect?

choices.text: It is a full mu-receptor agonist like morphine.
choices.note: No. Full mu agonism is the morphine line.

choices.text: It is an NSAID with the same anti-inflammatory line as indomethacin.
choices.note: No. Indomethacin is Indocid, an NSAID; the note denies an anti-inflammatory action for paracetamol.

choices.text: It is a local urinary analgesic that dyes the urine.
choices.note: No. Urine colour change is written for phenazopyridine (Pyridium).

choices.text: It inhibits central prostaglandin synthesis to lower fever and pain, and the note says it has no anti-inflammatory action.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, paracetamol inhibits central prostaglandin synthesis for fever and pain but has no anti-inflammatory effect.

scene: A nurse looks at Ultram on a moderate-to-severe pain chart.
ask: What mechanism does the note give tramadol?

choices.text: It only inhibits COX and is classed as an NSAID.
choices.note: No. COX inhibition is the NSAID mechanism, used for drugs such as diclofenac and naproxen.

choices.text: It is a local anaesthetic excreted in urine like phenazopyridine.
choices.note: No. Urinary local analgesia is the phenazopyridine line.

choices.text: Weak mu-receptor action plus inhibition of serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, tramadol has weak mu activity and inhibits 5-HT and noradrenaline reuptake.

choices.text: It blocks H1 receptors like a first-generation antihistamine.
choices.note: No. H1 blockade is the antihistamine mechanism, not tramadol.

scene: A nurse looks at Dologesic and Pyridium on two charts.
ask: Which description matches the note?

choices.text: Dologesic is morphine plus ibuprofen, and Pyridium is a loop diuretic.
choices.note: No. Morphine and ibuprofen are separate analgesics; loop diuresis is furosemide.

choices.text: Dologesic combines paracetamol with dextropropoxyphene; Pyridium is phenazopyridine and can turn urine orange-red.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Dologesic is paracetamol plus dextropropoxyphene, and phenazopyridine is a local urinary analgesic that can colour urine red-orange.

choices.text: Pyridium is aspirin and Dologesic is sucralfate.
choices.note: No. Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid and sucralfate is Carafate.

choices.text: Both are bulk-forming laxatives.
choices.note: No. The bulk-forming laxative is psyllium (Metamucil).

scene: A nurse looks at a teaching line about first- and second-generation antihistamines.
ask: How does the note contrast the two generations?

choices.text: First-generation drugs act in the CNS and periphery, cross the blood-brain barrier, and sedate; second-generation drugs act in the periphery and are written as non-sedating.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, first-generation antihistamines cross into the brain and sedate, while second-generation drugs stay peripheral and do not cause sleepiness.

choices.text: Second-generation drugs are the ones that cross the blood-brain barrier and cause sedation.
choices.note: No. The note assigns blood-brain barrier crossing and sedation to the first generation.

choices.text: Both generations are opioid antitussives.
choices.note: No. Opioid antitussive action is the codeine line, not this antihistamine contrast.

choices.text: First-generation drugs are glucocorticoids that inhibit phospholipase A2.
choices.note: No. Phospholipase A2 inhibition is the glucocorticoid mechanism.

scene: A nurse looks at Piriton on an allergy chart.
ask: What is Piriton in the note?

choices.text: Promethazine, a phenothiazine used only as an antiemetic.
choices.note: No. Promethazine is Phenergan/Phensedyl, a different first-generation antihistamine.

choices.text: Lorazepam, a benzodiazepine anxiolytic.
choices.note: No. Lorazepam is Ativan, a benzodiazepine.

choices.text: Haloperidol, a dopamine D2 blocker.
choices.note: No. Haloperidol is Haldol, a typical antipsychotic.

choices.text: Chlorpheniramine maleate, a first-generation non-selective antihistamine, for allergy, rhinitis, and hypersensitive reactions.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Piriton is chlorpheniramine, a first-generation H1 blocker for allergic symptoms, rhinitis, and hypersensitivity reactions including transfusion reactions.

scene: A nurse looks at Phenergan and Atarax on an antihistamine chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Both are second-generation non-sedating antihistamines.
choices.note: No. The note places both with first-generation H1 blockade and sedation.

choices.text: Atarax is furosemide and Phenergan is spironolactone.
choices.note: No. Furosemide is Lasix and spironolactone is Aldactone, diuretics rather than antihistamines.

choices.text: Phenergan is promethazine, an H1 blocker and phenothiazine; Atarax is hydroxyzine, an antihistamine with antianxiety, sedative, and antiemetic lines.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, promethazine and hydroxyzine are first-generation H1 antihistamines, and hydroxyzine is also classed for anxiety, sedation, and itch.

choices.text: Phenergan is salbutamol and Atarax is theophylline.
choices.note: No. Salbutamol is Ventolin and theophylline is the xanthine bronchodilator.

scene: A nurse looks at prednisolone and hydrocortisone on a steroid chart.
ask: How does the note compare them?

choices.text: Hydrocortisone is 4 to 5 times more anti-inflammatory than prednisolone and has no salt-retaining activity.
choices.note: No. The note sets hydrocortisone as the potency standard of 1 and gives prednisolone the higher anti-inflammatory figure.

choices.text: Prednisolone is a synthetic intermediate-acting glucocorticoid about 4 to 5 times hydrocortisone; hydrocortisone is the natural short-acting glucocorticoid with clearer salt-retaining activity.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, prednisolone is synthetic and about 4-5 times hydrocortisone in anti-inflammatory potency, while hydrocortisone is natural, short-acting, and stronger at retaining salt.

choices.text: Both are mineralocorticoids only, and prednisolone is fludrocortisone.
choices.note: No. Fludrocortisone is the mineralocorticoid example; prednisolone is a glucocorticoid.

choices.text: Prednisolone is an NSAID that inhibits COX and hydrocortisone is an antihistamine.
choices.note: No. COX inhibition is the NSAID line and H1 blockade is the antihistamine line.

scene: A nurse looks at a glucocorticoid mechanism line on an anti-inflammatory chart.
ask: What mechanism does the note write?

choices.text: They bind intracellular receptors, inhibit phospholipase A2 and COX-2, and reduce prostaglandins and leukotrienes.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, glucocorticoids inhibit phospholipase A2 and COX-2, lowering prostaglandins and leukotrienes, which the note links to anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressant effects.

choices.text: They block H1 receptors and do not affect prostaglandins.
choices.note: No. H1 blockade is the antihistamine mechanism.

choices.text: They inhibit Na/K-ATPase in cardiac muscle.
choices.note: No. Na/K-ATPase inhibition is the digoxin mechanism.

choices.text: They block angiotensin II receptors.
choices.note: No. Angiotensin II receptor blockade is the ARB mechanism.

scene: A nurse looks at fludrocortisone beside an adrenal-failure note.
ask: What class and use does the note give fludrocortisone?

choices.text: A loop diuretic that wastes sodium.
choices.note: No. Sodium wasting on the thick ascending limb is the loop diuretic action.

choices.text: An inhaled corticosteroid identical to budesonide.
choices.note: No. Budesonide is Pulmicort, an inhaled glucocorticoid in the respiratory section.

choices.text: A first-generation antihistamine for rhinitis.
choices.note: No. Rhinitis antihistamines here include chlorpheniramine and promethazine.

choices.text: A mineralocorticoid that promotes sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion, written for Addison's disease.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, fludrocortisone is the mineralocorticoid example for Addison's disease, retaining sodium and water.

scene: A nurse looks at Ativan on an anxiety chart.
ask: What class and receptor action does the note give Ativan?

choices.text: Haloperidol, a butyrophenone that blocks D2 receptors.
choices.note: No. D2 blockade is the Haldol (haloperidol) line.

choices.text: An opioid that binds mu receptors.
choices.note: No. Mu-receptor binding is the opioid analgesic mechanism.

choices.text: Lorazepam, a benzodiazepine that enhances GABA, increases chloride entry, and hyperpolarises neurons.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Ativan (lorazepam) boosts GABA, increases chloride inflow, and is used for anxiety, insomnia, preoperative sedation, and seizures.

choices.text: Trihexyphenidyl, an anticholinergic for Parkinson symptoms.
choices.note: No. Trihexyphenidyl is Artane, not lorazepam.

scene: A nurse looks at Haldol on a psychosis chart.
ask: What does the note say Haldol does at receptors?

choices.text: It is a benzodiazepine that promotes GABA-A chloride flow.
choices.note: No. GABA-A chloride flow is the lorazepam mechanism.

choices.text: Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic (butyrophenone) that blocks D2 receptors and lowers dopamine activity.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Haldol (haloperidol) is a D2 blocker for psychosis, agitation, and vomiting, not a GABA-A benzodiazepine.

choices.text: It is trihexyphenidyl, an anticholinergic for Parkinson disease.
choices.note: No. Trihexyphenidyl is Artane.

choices.text: It is levodopa, a dopamine precursor.
choices.note: No. Levodopa is the dopamine precursor in Sinemet.

scene: A nurse looks at the chart note that pairs the letters A and H with two drugs.
ask: What memory line does the note give?

choices.text: A is Calm Anxiety for Ativan; H is Halt Hallucination for Haldol.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Ativan is linked to calming anxiety and Haldol to halting hallucination.

choices.text: A is Halt Hallucination for Ativan and H is Calm Anxiety for Haldol.
choices.note: No. The note pairs A with anxiety (Ativan) and H with hallucination (Haldol).

choices.text: Both letters refer to the antihistamines Piriton and Phenergan.
choices.note: No. Piriton and Phenergan are antihistamines, not this A/H memory line.

choices.text: A is allopurinol and H is hydrochlorothiazide.
choices.note: No. Allopurinol is Zyloric and hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic, not this pair.

scene: A nurse looks at Doxil and Blenoxane on an oncology chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Doxil is cisplatin and Blenoxane is tamoxifen.
choices.note: No. Cisplatin is an alkylating agent and tamoxifen is the hormone antagonist for estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer.

choices.text: Both are vinca alkaloids that stop microtubules.
choices.note: No. Microtubule inhibition is the vinblastine and vincristine line.

choices.text: Doxil is methotrexate and Blenoxane is fluorouracil.
choices.note: No. Methotrexate and fluorouracil are the antimetabolites.

choices.text: Doxil is doxorubicin and Blenoxane is bleomycin; both are anti-neoplastic antibiotics against rapidly proliferating malignant cells.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, doxorubicin (Doxil) and bleomycin (Blenoxane) are anti-neoplastic antibiotics.

scene: A nurse looks at cisplatin, carboplatin, and Ifex on a chemotherapy chart.
ask: What class does the note give these three?

choices.text: They are antitumour antibiotics like doxorubicin.
choices.note: No. Doxorubicin and bleomycin are the anti-neoplastic antibiotics.

choices.text: They are hormone antagonists, and cisplatin is tamoxifen.
choices.note: No. Tamoxifen is the anti-neoplastic written for estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer.

choices.text: Anti-neoplastic alkylating agents; Ifex is ifosfamide, and carboplatin is written for initial treatment of ovarian cancer.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, cisplatin, carboplatin, and ifosfamide (Ifex) are alkylating anti-neoplastic agents.

choices.text: They are vinca alkaloids, and Ifex is vincristine.
choices.note: No. Vincristine is the miscellaneous vinca alkaloid, not ifosfamide.

scene: A nurse looks at methotrexate and fluorouracil on an oncology chart.
ask: How does the note class them?

choices.text: Both are alkylating agents used only for initial ovarian cancer.
choices.note: No. Initial ovarian cancer is the carboplatin line; these two are antimetabolites.

choices.text: Both are anti-neoplastic antimetabolites against rapidly proliferating malignant cells, and methotrexate is also written for psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, methotrexate and fluorouracil are antimetabolites; methotrexate is also listed for psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis.

choices.text: Methotrexate is bleomycin and fluorouracil is doxorubicin.
choices.note: No. Bleomycin is Blenoxane and doxorubicin is Doxil, the antibiotic anti-neoplastics.

choices.text: Both are vinca alkaloids that block mitosis.
choices.note: No. Mitotic spindle blockade is the vinca alkaloid mechanism.

scene: A nurse looks at tamoxifen, vinblastine, and vincristine on a cancer chart.
ask: Which uses match the note?

choices.text: Tamoxifen is written for advanced estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer; vinblastine and vincristine are anti-neoplastics, and vincristine is classed as miscellaneous.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, tamoxifen is for estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer, and vinblastine and vincristine are anti-neoplastic agents, with vincristine marked miscellaneous.

choices.text: Tamoxifen is an alkylating agent for testicular cancer only.
choices.note: No. Testicular cancer appears with several cytotoxics, but tamoxifen is the hormone-directed breast-cancer drug.

choices.text: All three are anti-neoplastic antibiotics.
choices.note: No. The antibiotic anti-neoplastics named are doxorubicin and bleomycin.

choices.text: Vincristine is tamoxifen and vinblastine is ifosfamide.
choices.note: No. Ifosfamide is Ifex, an alkylating agent.

scene: A nurse looks at mechanism lines for doxorubicin, cisplatin, and fluorouracil.
ask: Which mechanism set matches the note?

choices.text: All three block estrogen receptors.
choices.note: No. Estrogen-receptor blockade is the tamoxifen line.

choices.text: Cisplatin inhibits microtubule assembly and doxorubicin is a hormone antagonist.
choices.note: No. Microtubule assembly is the vinca line, and the hormone antagonist named is tamoxifen.

choices.text: Fluorouracil is a vinca alkaloid that stops the mitotic spindle.
choices.note: No. The mitotic-spindle drugs are vinblastine and vincristine.

choices.text: Doxorubicin binds DNA and inhibits DNA and RNA synthesis; cisplatin cross-links DNA; fluorouracil imitates a nucleotide and inhibits DNA synthesis.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, antitumour antibiotics such as doxorubicin bind DNA, alkylators such as cisplatin cross-link DNA, and antimetabolites such as fluorouracil mimic nucleotides to block DNA synthesis.

scene: A nurse looks at vinblastine and vincristine on a spindle diagram.
ask: How does the note say vinca alkaloids work?

choices.text: They cross-link DNA like alkylating agents.
choices.note: No. DNA cross-linking is the alkylating-agent mechanism, as with cisplatin.

choices.text: They block estrogen receptors like tamoxifen.
choices.note: No. Estrogen-receptor blockade is the tamoxifen mechanism.

choices.text: They inhibit microtubule polymerisation and stop cells in the mitotic M phase.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, vinca alkaloids act on the mitotic spindle, inhibit microtubule assembly, and block M phase.

choices.text: They inhibit phosphodiesterase in bronchial muscle.
choices.note: No. Phosphodiesterase inhibition is the theophylline mechanism.

scene: A nurse looks at Blenoxane beside a DNA note.
ask: What does the note say bleomycin does to DNA?

choices.text: It blocks estrogen receptors in breast cancer.
choices.note: No. Estrogen-receptor blockade is written for tamoxifen.

choices.text: It causes DNA strand breaks and thereby stops proliferation.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, bleomycin causes DNA chain breaks, unlike the estrogen-receptor block written for tamoxifen.

choices.text: It inhibits microtubules in M phase like vincristine.
choices.note: No. Microtubule inhibition is the vinca alkaloid mechanism.

choices.text: It is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor for gout.
choices.note: No. Xanthine oxidase inhibition is the allopurinol and febuxostat line.

scene: A nurse looks at Zyloric on a chronic gout chart.
ask: What is Zyloric, and what enzyme does the note say it inhibits?

choices.text: Allopurinol, a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that lowers uric acid synthesis for chronic gout.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Zyloric (allopurinol) inhibits xanthine oxidase, decreases uric acid formation, and is for chronic gout and hyperuricaemia.

choices.text: Colchicine, a microtubule inhibitor for acute joint inflammation.
choices.note: No. Colchicine is Colgout, the microtubule inhibitor, not Zyloric.

choices.text: Probenecid, a uricosuric that increases uric acid excretion.
choices.note: No. Probenecid is the uricosuric, not the xanthine oxidase inhibitor.

choices.text: Tranexamic acid, a haemostatic antifibrinolytic.
choices.note: No. Tranexamic acid is Transamin/Cyklokapron, a haemostatic.

scene: A nurse looks at Uloric and Colgout on a gout chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Uloric is probenecid and Colgout is allopurinol.
choices.note: No. Probenecid is a uricosuric and allopurinol is Zyloric.

choices.text: Both are uricosuric agents that block uric acid reabsorption.
choices.note: No. Blocking uric acid reabsorption is the uricosuric mechanism of probenecid and sulfinpyrazone.

choices.text: Colgout is tranexamic acid and Uloric is warfarin.
choices.note: No. Tranexamic acid is the haemostatic and warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant.

choices.text: Uloric is febuxostat, another xanthine oxidase inhibitor; Colgout is colchicine, which inhibits microtubules and leukocyte migration into the joint.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, febuxostat inhibits xanthine oxidase and colchicine inhibits microtubule polymerisation to reduce joint inflammation.

scene: A nurse looks at probenecid and sulfinpyrazone on a chronic gout chart.
ask: What class and mechanism does the note give them?

choices.text: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors that stop uric acid being formed.
choices.note: No. Stopping uric acid formation is allopurinol and febuxostat.

choices.text: Microtubule inhibitors used for acute gout inflammation.
choices.note: No. The microtubule inhibitor for gout is colchicine.

choices.text: Uricosuric agents that inhibit uric acid reabsorption in the renal tubule so more uric acid is excreted.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, probenecid and sulfinpyrazone are uricosurics that block tubular reabsorption of uric acid.

choices.text: Loop diuretics that inhibit Na-K-2Cl transport.
choices.note: No. Na-K-2Cl inhibition is the loop diuretic mechanism of furosemide.

scene: A nurse looks at Transamin and Cyklokapron on a bleeding chart.
ask: What drug and action does the note give these brands?

choices.text: Both are warfarin, a vitamin K antagonist.
choices.note: No. Warfarin is Warfarin Norton, the vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant.

choices.text: Both are tranexamic acid, a haemostatic that inhibits plasmin and slows clot breakdown.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Transamin and Cyklokapron are tranexamic acid, inhibiting plasmin so clots are not dissolved and rebleeding is reduced.

choices.text: Both are enoxaparin, a low-molecular-weight heparin.
choices.note: No. Enoxaparin is Clexane, the low-molecular-weight heparin.

choices.text: Both are allopurinol, a xanthine oxidase inhibitor.
choices.note: No. Allopurinol is Zyloric, the xanthine oxidase inhibitor.

scene: A nurse looks at Warfarin Norton on an anticoagulant chart.
ask: What does the note say warfarin does?

choices.text: Warfarin sodium inhibits synthesis of vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX, and X, and is written for DVT, atrial fibrillation, embolisation, and myocardial infarction.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, warfarin is a vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant affecting factors II, VII, IX, and X.

choices.text: It is an antiplatelet ADP-receptor blocker like clopidogrel.
choices.note: No. ADP-receptor blockade is the clopidogrel (Plavix) line.

choices.text: It inhibits factor Xa through antithrombin III like enoxaparin.
choices.note: No. Antithrombin III and factor Xa are the enoxaparin (Clexane) mechanism.

choices.text: It raises platelet cAMP like dipyridamole and is not called an anticoagulant.
choices.note: No. Raising platelet cAMP is the dipyridamole line; warfarin is the anticoagulant.

scene: A nurse looks at Clexane and Plavix on a clot-prevention chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Clexane is warfarin and Plavix is tranexamic acid.
choices.note: No. Warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist and tranexamic acid is the haemostatic.

choices.text: Both are xanthine oxidase inhibitors.
choices.note: No. Xanthine oxidase inhibitors in the note are allopurinol and febuxostat.

choices.text: Plavix is heparin and Clexane is dipyridamole.
choices.note: No. Dipyridamole is Persantin; Clexane is the heparin product enoxaparin.

choices.text: Clexane is enoxaparin, a low-molecular-weight heparin that boosts antithrombin III and inhibits factor Xa; Plavix is clopidogrel, which blocks the platelet ADP receptor.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, enoxaparin is LMWH acting through antithrombin III on factor Xa, and clopidogrel blocks ADP receptors on platelets.

scene: A nurse looks at Persantin beside a heart-valve note.
ask: What antiplatelet mechanism does the note give dipyridamole?

choices.text: It inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.
choices.note: No. Those factors are the warfarin mechanism.

choices.text: It blocks the platelet ADP receptor like clopidogrel.
choices.note: No. ADP-receptor blockade is clopidogrel (Plavix).

choices.text: It inhibits platelet uptake of adenosine, raises cAMP inside platelets, and inhibits aggregation; the note also calls it a vasodilator.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Persantin (dipyridamole) raises platelet cAMP by inhibiting adenosine uptake and is used with warfarin for valve-related thromboembolism.

choices.text: It inhibits plasmin like tranexamic acid.
choices.note: No. Plasmin inhibition is the tranexamic acid mechanism.

scene: A nurse looks at vitamin B1 and B6 indications on a chart.
ask: Which uses match the note?

choices.text: Both are statins that inhibit HMG-CoA reductase.
choices.note: No. HMG-CoA reductase inhibition is the simvastatin (Zocor) line.

choices.text: Thiamine is written for polyneuritis, optic neuropathy, and cardiovascular disease; pyridoxine is written for B6 deficiency, seizures, and isoniazid therapy.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, thiamine (B1) is tied to polyneuritis and cardiovascular disease, and pyridoxine (B6) is tied to isoniazid therapy and neuropathy.

choices.text: Pyridoxine is calcium carbonate and thiamine is sodium polystyrene sulfonate.
choices.note: No. Calcium carbonate is Oscal/Caltrate and sodium polystyrene sulfonate is Resonium A.

choices.text: Thiamine is the antidote named for warfarin overdose.
choices.note: No. The note names vitamin K1 (phytonadione) for warfarin excess.

scene: A nurse looks at folic acid and Oscal on a supplement chart.
ask: What does the note say these are?

choices.text: Folic acid is vitamin B9 for folate deficiency and pregnancy; Oscal/Caltrate is calcium carbonate, an antacid and calcium supplement, with a line saying not for chronic therapy.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, folic acid is vitamin B9 for deficiency and pregnancy, and Oscal/Caltrate is CaCO3, an antacid and calcium supplement, with the phrase not for chronic therapy.

choices.text: Oscal is simvastatin and folic acid is a loop diuretic.
choices.note: No. Simvastatin is Zocor and the loop diuretic is furosemide.

choices.text: Both are HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors taken at night.
choices.note: No. Night-time dosing in the note is the statin (simvastatin) point.

choices.text: Folic acid is vitamin B1 and Oscal is sodium polystyrene sulfonate.
