choices.note: No. Vitamin B1 is thiamine and the potassium-binding resin is Resonium A.

scene: A nurse looks at Zocor on a cholesterol chart.
ask: What class and lipid effects does the note give Zocor?

choices.text: It is warfarin and it inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors.
choices.note: No. Vitamin K-dependent factors are the warfarin mechanism.

choices.text: It is allopurinol and it lowers uric acid rather than LDL.
choices.note: No. Lowering uric acid synthesis is allopurinol.

choices.text: It is tranexamic acid and it inhibits plasmin.
choices.note: No. Plasmin inhibition is tranexamic acid, not simvastatin.

choices.text: Simvastatin, an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that lowers LDL and triglycerides and raises HDL.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Zocor (simvastatin) inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, decreases LDL and triglycerides, and increases HDL.

scene: A nurse looks at Dequadin and Strepsils on a sore-throat chart.
ask: How does the note class these throat preparations?

choices.text: Both are systemic penicillins, and Dequadin is amoxicillin.
choices.note: No. Amoxicillin is Amoxil, a penicillin, not a throat lozenge.

choices.text: Strepsils is codeine and Dequadin is dextromethorphan.
choices.note: No. Codeine and dextromethorphan are cough suppressants in the respiratory section.

choices.text: Dequadin is dequalinium chloride, a quaternary-ammonium antiseptic lozenge; Strepsils contains dichlorobenzyl alcohol and amylmetacresol.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Dequadin is dequalinium and Strepsils is dichlorobenzyl alcohol plus amylmetacresol for mouth and throat infection or sore throat.

choices.text: Both are proton pump inhibitors for ulcer pain.
choices.note: No. Proton pump inhibitors are the -zole antiulcer drugs.

scene: A nurse looks at Resonium A on a high-potassium chart.
ask: What is Resonium A, and how does the note say it lowers potassium?

choices.text: It is calcium carbonate, an antacid.
choices.note: No. Calcium carbonate is Oscal/Caltrate.

choices.text: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate, a resin that exchanges sodium for potassium in the gut so potassium leaves the body.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, Resonium A is sodium polystyrene sulfonate for hyperkalaemia, swapping Na for K in the intestine.

choices.text: It is activated charcoal, which adsorbs many oral poisons.
choices.note: No. Activated charcoal is the adsorbent antidote, not the potassium resin.

choices.text: It is naloxone, an opioid antagonist.
choices.note: No. Naloxone is the opioid antagonist in the detoxifying list.

scene: A nurse looks at a route note beside Resonium A.
ask: Which routes does the note allow for Resonium A?

choices.text: By mouth or as an enema.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, sodium polystyrene sulfonate may be given orally or by enema for hyperkalaemia.

choices.text: Only as an intravenous bolus.
choices.note: No. The note gives oral and enema routes, not an intravenous bolus.

choices.text: Only as an inhaled bronchodilator.
choices.note: No. Inhaled bronchodilators in the note include salbutamol and ipratropium.

choices.text: Only as a throat lozenge like Dequadin.
choices.note: No. Dequadin is the throat lozenge; Resonium A is the potassium resin.

scene: A nurse looks at activated charcoal, N-acetylcysteine, and naloxone on an antidote chart.
ask: Which poison match matches the note?

choices.text: Naloxone is for benzodiazepines, NAC is for iron, and charcoal is for cyanide.
choices.note: No. Benzodiazepines map to flumazenil, iron to deferoxamine, and cyanide to hydroxocobalamin.

choices.text: All three reactivate acetylcholinesterase in organophosphate poisoning.
choices.note: No. Acetylcholinesterase reactivation is the pralidoxime line.

choices.text: Charcoal is vitamin K for warfarin, and naloxone is deferoxamine.
choices.note: No. Vitamin K1 is for warfarin and deferoxamine is the iron chelator.

choices.text: Activated charcoal adsorbs many oral poisons; N-acetylcysteine is the paracetamol antidote; naloxone reverses opioid effects such as heroin or morphine overdose.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, charcoal is an adsorbent, NAC supplies a glutathione precursor in paracetamol poisoning, and naloxone competes at opioid receptors.

scene: A nurse looks at atropine, pralidoxime, flumazenil, and vitamin K1 on an antidote chart.
ask: Which pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Flumazenil is the opioid antidote and vitamin K1 is for paracetamol.
choices.note: No. The opioid antidote is naloxone and the paracetamol antidote is N-acetylcysteine.

choices.text: Pralidoxime is for iron overload and atropine is simvastatin.
choices.note: No. Iron overload is deferoxamine and simvastatin is the statin Zocor.

choices.text: Atropine and pralidoxime (2-PAM) are for organophosphate poisoning; flumazenil blocks the benzodiazepine site; vitamin K1 (phytonadione) is for warfarin excess.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, atropine plus 2-PAM is the organophosphate pair, flumazenil antagonises benzodiazepines at GABA-A, and vitamin K1 is for warfarin over-anticoagulation.

choices.text: All four are heavy-metal chelators.
choices.note: No. Heavy-metal chelators in the note include dimercaprol and EDTA.

scene: A nurse looks at deferoxamine, dimercaprol, EDTA, and hydroxocobalamin.
ask: Which poisoning match matches the note?

choices.text: EDTA is for cyanide, hydroxocobalamin is for lead, and deferoxamine is for opioids.
choices.note: No. The note pairs EDTA with lead, hydroxocobalamin with cyanide, and naloxone with opioids.

choices.text: Deferoxamine chelates iron; dimercaprol (BAL) is for arsenic, mercury, and gold; EDTA is for lead; hydroxocobalamin binds cyanide.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, deferoxamine is the iron chelator, BAL chelates arsenic, mercury, and gold, calcium disodium edetate is for lead, and hydroxocobalamin is a cyanide antidote.

choices.text: Dimercaprol is vitamin K and EDTA is naloxone.
choices.note: No. Vitamin K1 is phytonadione and naloxone is the opioid antagonist.

choices.text: All four are used only for paracetamol overdose.
choices.note: No. Paracetamol overdose in this table is N-acetylcysteine.

scene: A nurse looks at a table matching antibiotics to bacterial targets.
ask: Which target pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Beta-lactams inhibit cell-wall synthesis; macrolides act on the 50S ribosome; aminoglycosides act on the 30S ribosome; fluoroquinolones inhibit DNA gyrase.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, beta-lactams attack the wall, macrolides hit 50S, streptomycin-type aminoglycosides hit 30S, and fluoroquinolones stop DNA gyrase.

choices.text: Macrolides inhibit cell-wall synthesis and beta-lactams inhibit DNA gyrase.
choices.note: No. The note gives the wall to beta-lactams and DNA gyrase to fluoroquinolones.

choices.text: Fluoroquinolones bind the 50S ribosome and metronidazole is an aminoglycoside.
choices.note: No. 50S is the macrolide target; metronidazole is written against anaerobic DNA, and streptomycin is the aminoglycoside.

choices.text: Aminoglycosides inhibit mycolic acid synthesis like isoniazid.
choices.note: No. Mycolic acid inhibition is the isoniazid line, not the aminoglycoside 30S line.

scene: A nurse looks at Klacid, Zinnat, Amoxil, and Flagyl on an infection chart.
ask: Which identities match the note?

choices.text: Klacid is streptomycin, Zinnat is ciprofloxacin, Amoxil is metronidazole, and Flagyl is erythromycin.
choices.note: No. Those classes are in the note, but the brands do not pair that way.

choices.text: All four are fluoroquinolones, and Flagyl is ciprofloxacin.
choices.note: No. Ciprofloxacin is Cipro, a fluoroquinolone; Flagyl is metronidazole.

choices.text: Zinnat is isoniazid and Klacid is ethambutol.
choices.note: No. Isoniazid is Rimifon and ethambutol is Myambutol, anti-tubercular drugs.

choices.text: Klacid is clarithromycin, a macrolide; Zinnat is oral cefuroxime, a second-generation cephalosporin; Amoxil is amoxicillin, a penicillin; Flagyl is metronidazole.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, clarithromycin is a macrolide, cefuroxime is a second-generation cephalosporin (Zinnat by mouth, Zinacef by vein), amoxicillin is a penicillin, and metronidazole is Flagyl.

scene: A nurse looks at erythromycin and Augmentin on an antibiotic chart.
ask: What mechanisms does the note give?

choices.text: Erythromycin inhibits DNA gyrase and Augmentin is salbutamol plus fluticasone.
choices.note: No. DNA gyrase is the fluoroquinolone target, and salbutamol plus fluticasone is not this antibiotic pair.

choices.text: Both inhibit mycolic acid synthesis like isoniazid.
choices.note: No. Mycolic acid synthesis is the isoniazid mechanism.

choices.text: Erythromycin inhibits the 50S ribosomal subunit; Augmentin is amoxicillin plus clavulanic acid, the penicillin inhibiting the cell wall and clavulanic acid inhibiting beta-lactamase.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, erythromycin blocks 50S protein synthesis and Augmentin pairs amoxicillin with the beta-lactamase inhibitor clavulanic acid.

choices.text: Augmentin is cefuroxime alone and erythromycin binds fungal ergosterol.
choices.note: No. Cefuroxime is Zinnat/Zinacef, and ergosterol binding is the nystatin line.

scene: A nurse looks at cloxacillin and Flagyl on a chart.
ask: What special coverage does the note write?

choices.text: Cloxacillin binds the 30S ribosome and Flagyl is a macrolide.
choices.note: No. 30S binding is streptomycin, and macrolides include erythromycin and clarithromycin.

choices.text: Cloxacillin is a beta-lactamase-resistant penicillin for gram-positive organisms such as staphylococci; metronidazole damages DNA and is written for anaerobes and protozoa.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, cloxacillin resists beta-lactamase, and Flagyl (metronidazole) disrupts DNA in anaerobic bacteria and protozoa.

choices.text: Both are fluoroquinolones that only inhibit DNA gyrase.
choices.note: No. DNA gyrase inhibition is ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin.

choices.text: Flagyl is acyclovir, a guanine analogue for herpes.
choices.note: No. Acyclovir is the antiviral guanine analogue, not metronidazole.

scene: A nurse looks at Cipro, levofloxacin, and streptomycin.
ask: Which class lines match the note?

choices.text: Ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin are fluoroquinolones that inhibit DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; streptomycin is an aminoglycoside that binds the 30S ribosome and is also anti-tuberculosis.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, the fluoroquinolones block DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, and streptomycin binds 30S and is listed as an anti-tuberculosis antibiotic.

choices.text: All three only inhibit cell-wall cross-linking like penicillins.
choices.note: No. Cell-wall cross-linking is the beta-lactam mechanism.

choices.text: Streptomycin is a macrolide on the 50S subunit and ciprofloxacin is metronidazole.
choices.note: No. 50S is the macrolide target and metronidazole is Flagyl.

choices.text: Levofloxacin is nystatin and ciprofloxacin is rifampicin.
choices.note: No. Nystatin is Mycostatin and rifampicin is Rifadin/Rimactane.

scene: A nurse looks at Rimifon, Rifadin, Myambutol, and Tebrazid on a tuberculosis chart.
ask: Which generic pairing matches the note?

choices.text: Rimifon is rifampicin, Myambutol is isoniazid, and Tebrazid is streptomycin.
choices.note: No. The note pairs Rimifon with isoniazid, Myambutol with ethambutol, and streptomycin is a separate antibiotic.

choices.text: All four are penicillins, and Rimifon is amoxicillin.
choices.note: No. Amoxicillin is Amoxil, a penicillin, not an anti-tubercular brand.

choices.text: Tebrazid is acyclovir and Myambutol is nystatin.
choices.note: No. Acyclovir is the antiviral and nystatin is Mycostatin.

choices.text: Rimifon is isoniazid, Rifadin/Rimactane is rifampicin, Myambutol is ethambutol, and Tebrazid is pyrazinamide.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, the anti-tubercular set is isoniazid, rifampicin (rifampin), ethambutol, and pyrazinamide under those brand names.

scene: A nurse looks at mechanism lines for the four main anti-tubercular drugs.
ask: Which mechanism set matches the note?

choices.text: All four inhibit cell-wall peptidoglycan cross-linking like penicillins.
choices.note: No. Peptidoglycan cross-linking is the beta-lactam mechanism.

choices.text: Ethambutol binds ergosterol and pyrazinamide inhibits viral DNA polymerase.
choices.note: No. Ergosterol binding is nystatin and viral DNA polymerase is acyclovir.

choices.text: Isoniazid inhibits mycolic acid synthesis; rifampicin inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase; ethambutol inhibits arabinosyl transferase; pyrazinamide interferes with lipid metabolism and membrane transport.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, INH blocks mycolic acid and should never be used alone, rifampicin blocks RNA polymerase, ethambutol blocks arabinosyl transferase, and pyrazinamide disturbs lipid metabolism and membrane transport.

choices.text: Rifampicin inhibits DNA gyrase and isoniazid is metronidazole.
choices.note: No. DNA gyrase is the fluoroquinolone target and metronidazole is Flagyl.

scene: A nurse looks at acyclovir and Mycostatin on an infection chart.
ask: Which mechanisms match the note?

choices.text: Acyclovir binds ergosterol and nystatin inhibits mycolic acid.
choices.note: No. Ergosterol is the nystatin target and mycolic acid is the isoniazid target.

choices.text: Acyclovir is a guanine analogue that inhibits viral DNA polymerase for herpes simplex and varicella-zoster; Mycostatin is nystatin, which binds fungal ergosterol and disrupts the membrane.
choices.note: Correct. As the note writes it, acyclovir stops viral DNA polymerase and nystatin binds ergosterol; nystatin is for local or oral candida, not systemic fungal infection.

choices.text: Both are anti-tubercular drugs, and Mycostatin is ethambutol.
choices.note: No. Ethambutol is Myambutol, an anti-tubercular drug.

choices.text: Nystatin inhibits DNA gyrase and acyclovir is clavulanic acid.
choices.note: No. DNA gyrase is the fluoroquinolone target and clavulanic acid is the beta-lactamase inhibitor in Augmentin.
